metrics.title: Full-history hyperbolic Frechet query against the whole level-1 cell set, scored by a temperatured Plackett-Luce expected rank and normalised by the size-matched prior.
metrics.formula:
Let K = 256 level-1 codes. Let I be the items of the TRAINING split, N = |I|. For i in I, b(i) in {1,...,K} is its level-1 code from the exported SID table; x_i (source) and y_i (target) are the frozen reference's representations in the Poincare ball B^d_c of curvature -c, with c = c_ref and tau = tau_ref read from the frozen reference (never fitted). Put Bs = {b : n_b > 0}, n_b = |{i in I : b(i) = b}|, w_b = n_b / N.
Frechet barycentre of a finite set S: m(S) = argmin_z sum_{u in S} d_c(z,u)^2, computed as the Lorentzian centroid by fixed-point iteration (not a Euclidean mean).
Query: q_h = m({x_j : j in history(h)}) for every training history h.
Cell prototype: mu_b = m({y_i : i in I, b(i) = b}) for every b in Bs.
Lorentz lift: L(z) = ( (1 + c||z||^2)/(1 - c||z||^2), 2z/(1 - c||z||^2) ) / sqrt(c); Minkowski product <u,v>_L = -u_0 v_0 + sum_{k=1..d} u_k v_k.
Logit: z_b(h) = <L(q_h), L(mu_b)>_L / tau.
Cell softmax: p_b(h) = exp(z_b(h)) / sum_{b' in Bs} exp(z_{b'}(h)).
Observed expected rank of the true cell b+(h): ER_obs(h) = 1 + sum_{b in Bs, b != b+(h)} p_b(h) / (p_b(h) + p_{b+(h)}(h)).
Size-matched prior expected rank: ER_null(h) = 1 + sum_{b in Bs, b != b+(h)} w_b / (w_b + w_{b+(h)}).
Per-history gain: rho(h) = clip( (ER_null(h) - ER_obs(h)) / (ER_null(h) - 1), 0, 1 ), and rho(h) = 0 if ER_null(h) <= 1 + 1e-12.
METRIC = (1/|H|) sum_{h in H} rho(h), a single scalar in [0,1], higher = better.
metrics.inputs: the exported SID table (one integer level-1 code per item); the frozen Issue #126 behaviour reference (source x_i, target y_i per item, curvature c_ref, temperature tau_ref); the TRAINING split (histories and their positive next item). Nothing else; no validation interaction and no test interaction, and no recall value.
metrics.geometry: The space is the Poincare ball of fixed negative curvature -c (c = c_ref). Curvature enters three times. (1) q_h and every mu_b are Frechet barycentres under the Poincare geodesic d_c, i.e. exp/log-map means; a Euclidean centroid would move every point. (2) <L(q_h),L(mu_b)>_L = -cosh(sqrt(c) d_c(q_h, mu_b)), so every logit is a geodesic-distance comparison and the softmax bandwidth is fixed by c and tau together, not by a free kernel width. (3) The effective comparison is the tangent-space norm ||log_{q_h}(mu_b)|| = d_c(q_h, mu_b), which is only defined through the hyperbolic exponential map. No step is a Euclidean distance in disguise.
metrics.why: Stage-3 Recall@10 needs the true item's level-1 cell to be among the cells that the reference-driven retrieval surfaces, because a level-1 prefix mismatch removes the item from the candidate prefix. ER_obs is precisely the temperatured expected rank of the true cell among ALL 256 cell prototypes under the reference's own softmax, conditioned on the entire training history rather than on one item. The denominator ER_null is the expected rank the same true cell would get from its size alone, so rho measures the fraction of the size-prior rank penalty that the reference's hyperbolic geometry actually removes. That adds over Q_H (which scores the prefix by within-prefix ranking and never uses the reference geometry or the query history) and over HBAA (which reduces the negatives to one sampled i- and a pairwise sigmoid, so it is negative-sampling dependent and ignores the other 254 cells): here the full negative distribution is integrated with the reference temperature, and the size-matched null removes the free credit that made the plain path likelihood reward collapse.
metrics.compute: 256 Lorentz barycentres over about N/256 = 96 points each: O(50 * N * d); |H| history barycentres over average history length L: O(50 * |H| * L * d); per history 256 logits and 256 Plackett-Luce terms: O(|H| * K). With N = 24587, K = 256, d <= 128 and |H| <= N this is under 1e8 flops and a few seconds on one CPU; histories are processed in chunks so memory stays O(N). The 50 fixed-point steps are a numerical constant, not a tuned parameter.
metrics.risks: (a) if tau_ref is on a different scale from the Lorentz inner products, the softmax saturates (ER_obs -> 1 for every table) or flattens (ER_obs -> (B+1)/2), and the metric loses discrimination; (b) the hyperbolic Frechet mean is not robust, so a few boundary-near target outliers can drag mu_b; (c) source and target must live in the same ball, otherwise <L(q_h),L(mu_b)>_L is meaningless; (d) very short histories give a noisy q_h; (e) ER_null grows with the number of nonempty cells, so the ratio only partly removes a residual dependence on B; (f) if Stage 3 gates on full SIDs rather than level-1 prefixes, level-1 rank need not map to recall; (g) for extremely unbalanced cells ER_null can sit near 1, and the epsilon rule sends those histories to 0.
metrics.failure_mode: It must be worst on a SID table whose level-1 partition is a balanced random relabelling with all 256 cells nonempty and nearly equal n_b: then every mu_b collapses onto the global target mean, all 256 logits are equal, ER_obs = ER_null = (256+1)/2 = 128.5, the numerator is 0 and METRIC is 0. A one-code table also scores exactly 0 because Bs has one element and the denominator rule applies. It is deliberately not worst on a coarse but geodesically pure table, which is what prevents it from rewarding collapse.

metrics.title: Size-matched hyperbolic information gain of the full SID partition about the frozen reference's target distribution
metrics.formula:
Let V be the N=24587 items. Work in the Poincare ball B^3={x in R^3 : ||x||<1} with fixed curvature K=-1 and distance dP(x,y)=arcosh(1+2||x-y||^2/((1-||x||^2)(1-||y||^2))). The frozen Issue #126 reference gives, per item v, a source vector s_v in B^3, a target vector r_v in B^3, and its temperature tau. For each item i let H(i) be its training-split history (set of training items) and h_i the Karcher (Frechet) barycentre of {s_j : j in H(i)} in (B^3,dP), computed by the standard iteration h <- exp_h( mean_{j in H(i)} log_h(s_j) ). Define the reference predictive distribution
  p_i(v) = exp(-dP(h_i, r_v)/tau) / sum_{w in V} exp(-dP(h_i, r_w)/tau).
Let code(v) be the FULL SID tuple of v (all levels 1..L), partitioning V into C cells c with sizes n_c, sum_c n_c = N. Define
  P_i(c) = sum_{v : code(v)=c} p_i(v),   H_i = - sum_c P_i(c) ln P_i(c)   (0 ln 0 := 0).
Null: for r=1..R (R=8, fixed a priori), draw a uniformly random partition of V into cells with the SAME size multiset (random permutation of V, first n_1 items to cell 1, next n_2 to cell 2, ...), recompute P_i^(r)(c) and H_i^(r); set H_i^0 = (1/R) sum_r H_i^(r).
Let Q be the systematic sample of every 6th item id, |Q| = floor(N/6) = 4096. The metric is
  M = (1/|Q|) sum_{i in Q} [ H_i^0 - H_i ]   (nats; M=0 if H_i^0=H_i=0 for all i).
Higher M is better. tau = the reference's frozen temperature; if only distances are exported, tau = median over training pairs (a,b) of dP(s_a, r_b), frozen before any recall is read.
metrics.inputs: (1) the exported SID table, item id -> integer code per level; (2) the frozen Issue #126 reference arrays s_v and r_v for all items plus its temperature tau; (3) the training split, used only to build each item's history H(i). Nothing else.
metrics.geometry: curvature K=-1 enters twice. First, h_i is a Karcher barycentre in the ball, computed with exp/log maps; it is not a Euclidean mean of s_j, because the Poincare conformal factor weights points near the boundary differently. Second, the softmax is over the Poincare distance dP(h_i,r_v), which saturates as points approach the boundary, so the logit ordering and spacing are curvature-dependent. A flat-limit run at K=-1e-3 is the stated control, not a tuning knob.
metrics.why: Stage-3 beam search over codes succeeds when, given a query, the reference's plausible targets concentrate on few SID codes. M is exactly the excess entropy that the real code removes from the reference's full predictive distribution, relative to a random partition of identical granularity. It uses the entire distribution over all 24587 candidates (not a mean over ten negatives), the whole history barycentre as the query (not a single anchor), and all SID levels at once. Over Q_H it adds: (i) the full negative distribution instead of a summary; (ii) all levels without an informativeness mask, because the size-matched null absorbs depth automatically; (iii) an information-theoretic rather than prefix-ranking target. Over HBAA it is not an item-wise positive-vs-negative contrast at all; it is a partition-level mutual-information statistic. The null makes collapse unprofitable by construction: one cell gives H=0 for both terms; N unique codes give the same permutation of the p_i values under both terms; a random relabelling is the null and scores ~0.
metrics.compute: about 4096 x 24587 = 1.0e8 Poincare distances, plus R=8 scatter-add passes of the same size via reduceat after sorting items by cell id; roughly 20-40 s in chunked float32 numpy (or a few seconds on GPU), peaking near 1 GB with 256-query chunks. Well under a minute.
metrics.risks: if the frozen reference's softmax is nearly flat for most histories, H_i and H_i^0 both approach the same value and M ties near 0 across tables; small tau makes M noisy on very fine cells; the R=8 Monte Carlo null adds sampling noise; if the reference is effectively Euclidean (its reps far from the boundary), the hyperbolic and flat versions will agree and the curvature adds little; sparse histories make h_i close to s_i and reduce the query-side signal.
metrics.failure_mode: it must be worst on an anti-clustered table whose codes are assigned to split each reference neighbourhood as evenly as possible across cells, e.g. level-1 code = (rank of the item within its reference nearest-neighbour block) mod C. There H_i > H_i^0, so M < 0. The two degenerate ends are neutral, not rewarded: a single-cell table and an all-unique-code table both give M = 0, and a randomly relabelled table gives M = 0 by definition.

metrics.title: Entropy-normalised pointwise mutual information between the level-1 SID code and the history, measured with Poincare geodesics at the history's Frechet barycentre.
metrics.formula:
Ball B^d = {x in R^d : ||x||_2 < 1}, constant sectional curvature -1, c_curv = 1.
 Item map: p_i = s_i / (1 + ||s_i||_2) in B^d (radii differ, so the Poincare distance is not a monotone function of any Euclidean chord).
 Poincare distance: d(x,y) = arcosh( 1 + 2||x-y||_2^2 / ((1-||x||_2^2)(1-||y||_2^2)) ).
 Mobius addition: x (+) y = ((1 + 2<x,y> + ||y||^2) x + (1 - ||x||^2) y) / (1 + 2<x,y> + ||x||^2 ||y||^2).
 exp_x(v) = x (+) tanh(||v||_2/2) v/||v||_2 ;  log_x(y) = 2 artanh(||(-x)(+)y||_2) ((-x)(+)y)/||(-x)(+)y||_2.
 T = 1/sqrt(c_curv) = 1 (curvature length scale, fixed).
 Codes: c(i) in {1..K} = the level-1 column of the SID table; K = number of distinct level-1 codes present (K <= 256); n_k = #{i in I : c(i)=k}; N = |I| = 24587.
 Cell centres: m_k = Frechet (Karcher) barycentre of {p_j : c(j)=k}, i.e. the point with sum_{j: c(j)=k} log_{m_k}(p_j) = 0; computed by 20 fixed Karcher iterations m <- exp_m( (1/n_k) sum_j log_m(p_j) ), started from the Euclidean cell mean projected into B (20 is fixed, not tuned).
 History query: for every training interaction (u,t) with t >= 2, let H = the items at positions < t in user u's sequence and i = the item at position t; b = Frechet barycentre of {p_j : j in H}, computed by the running recursion b <- exp_b( (1/|H|) log_b(p_j) ) over H in sequence order.
 Leave-one-out positive centre: with k* = c(i), if n_{k*} >= 2 set m*_{k*} = exp_{m_{k*}}( -log_{m_{k*}}(p_i) / (n_{k*} - 1) ); if n_{k*} = 1 the interaction contributes exactly 0.
 Logits: l_k = -d(b, m_k)/T for k != k* ;  l_{k*} = -d(b, m*_{k*})/T.
 p_{k*} = exp(l_{k*}) / sum_{k=1..K} exp(l_k), with max subtraction.
 Per-interaction score: g = log p_{k*} - log(n_{k*}/N).
 Aggregate: M = number of training interactions with t >= 2; PMI = (1/M) sum_m g_m.
 Entropy: H1 = - sum_k (n_k/N) log(n_k/N).
 METRIC VALUE: S = PMI / H1 if H1 > 1e-9, else S = 0. One scalar, higher is better.
metrics.inputs: (1) the exported Stage-2 SID table, level-1 code column only (levels 2-4 unused); (2) the frozen Issue #126 reference SOURCE representations s_i in R^d for the 24587 items, trained on training pairs only; (3) the training split (user->item sequences), used only to define the histories H. Nothing else: no validation interaction, no test interaction, no recall, no Stage-3 artefact, no fitted quantity.
metrics.geometry: The score lives entirely in the Poincare ball of fixed curvature c_curv = 1 (sectional curvature -1). Curvature enters (a) through the Poincare distance d, which is not Euclidean: the conformal factor 2/(1-||x||^2) inside arcosh makes the same Euclidean gap far more costly near the boundary than near the origin, and items with larger reference norms sit nearer the boundary and get a steeper metric; (b) through exp/log and Mobius addition, which define every barycentre (the history query b and the K cell centres m_k) and the leave-one-out centre exp_m(-log_m(p_i)/(n-1)), a first-order Riemannian gradient step on the Frechet functional; (c) through the temperature T = 1/sqrt(c_curv), so the softmax is the heat kernel of the curved metric and ||log_b(m)||_b = d(b,m) is exactly the compared quantity. Points are NOT placed on a common sphere, so the ordering is not a re-expression of a Euclidean or cosine ranking.
metrics.why: Stage-3 Recall@10 asks whether a generator conditioned on the history emits the true next item's code within ten tries. That is governed by two things the table controls: is the level-1 code conditionally predictable from the history, and is the prefix fine enough to separate the true next item. S = PMI/H1 is the fraction of the level-1 code's entropy that the frozen reference geometry of the history can explain, so it estimates the first factor directly and divides out the second. What it adds over Q_H (+0.634) and HBAA (+0.701): (i) it replaces the mean over ten negatives with the full negative distribution -- the log softmax normaliser over all K <= 256 cells -- so a table that puts the true cell first with a flat posterior is separated from one that is confidently first; (ii) the explicit size-matched marginal log(n_k/N) makes the score a calibrated gain over a size-only baseline rather than a raw likelihood, so a coarse table is capped at log 2 and is never paid for branching less, which is exactly the defect that drove the path likelihood to -0.488 with the 2/3/12-code tables at the top; (iii) the leave-one-out positive centre removes the item's own representation from its cell mean, so a table cannot buy score by shrinking cells towards singletons, i.e. by turning the level-1 prefix into an item identifier -- the mechanism that killed Q_H at levels 2 and 3; (iv) the query is the Frechet barycentre of the whole history, so the quantity is conditional predictability, not a marginal score. HBAA measures a signed margin along one direction from the mean of negatives; this measures a normalised log-evidence ratio against the whole negative mass, on a size-matched scale, with the item's own point removed.
metrics.compute: N = 24587 items, K <= 256 cells, reference dimension d (order 64-256), M training interactions. Item map O(N d). The K cell Frechet means are 20 passes over N points, about 5e8 multiply-adds. History barycentres are one exp/log step per interaction, O(M d). The logits need d(b, m_k) for all K cells, computed as batched pairwise Poincare distances with precomputed squared norms: about M x K x d multiply-adds, roughly 2e9 at M = 1e5, d = 64, which BLAS does in a few seconds with chunking to bound memory at M x K floats (about 100 MB at M = 1e5). The leave-one-out centre is closed form, O(d) per interaction. Total well under a minute, one pass, no optimisation, no training.
metrics.risks: (a) Low variance: if the reference source geometry is close to isotropic with respect to the level-1 partition, every table sits near PMI = 0 and the Spearman is noise -- the same failure that produced -0.081 and +0.156; the first diagnostic is the spread of S across the 97 tables. (b) Softmax saturation: if source norms are large, all p_i crowd the boundary, distances blow up and the softmax degenerates to argmax, making S coarse; the fixed T = 1 in ball units should be checked against realised distances being O(1). (c) A single dominant cell acts as a gravity well and makes PMI negative for items outside it -- intended, since that table is genuinely bad, but it can produce a bimodal distribution. (d) M = 0 if all training sequences have length 1, in which case S = 0. (e) For 2-3 code tables H1 is small and the ratio is noisy, which is the reason for the H1 > 1e-9 guard. (f) The metric inherits whatever the reference's source space gets wrong; a collapsed reference flattens S.
metrics.failure_mode: It must be worst, and is exactly 0, on the table that gives every item its own level-1 code (all n_k = 1, every contribution is 0 by the leave-one-out rule) and on the one-code table (K = 1, log(n/N) = 0 and the only logit is a constant, so S = 0). Among non-degenerate tables it is worst on a size-matched random relabelling of a good partition: preserving the cell sizes but destroying the geometry gives p_{k*} = n_{k*}/N, hence g = 0 for every interaction and S = 0, with any residual being negative finite-sample noise. Those are the three tables on which the construction cannot be gamed.

metrics.title: Lorentz-hyperboloid posterior-mass lift of the level-1 cell above its training prior (a curvature-exact PMI between the frozen reference and the code).
metrics.formula:
Setup. Items i = 1..N (N = 24587). The table gives level-1 code c1(i) in {1..K}, K <= 256. The frozen Issue #126 reference gives one Euclidean per-item representation x_i in R^d (its source side) and one frozen scalar temperature tau > 0. Fix curvature kappa = 1; nothing is fitted.
  (1) Map.  y_i = tanh(tau*||x_i||) * x_i/||x_i||  (the exp map exp_0(tau x_i) of the unit Poincare ball; y_i = 0 if ||x_i|| = 0).  Lift to the Lorentz hyperboloid:  p_i = ( (1+||y_i||^2)/(1-||y_i||^2) , 2*y_i/(1-||y_i||^2) )  in R^{d+1}.
  (2) Metric.  <a,b>_L = -a_0*b_0 + sum_{k=1..d} a_k*b_k  (Minkowski form, signature (-,+...+) ).  For lifted points <p_i,p_j>_L = -cosh(d_H(i,j)), where d_H is the unit-curvature hyperbolic (Poincare) distance.  So <p_i,p_j>_L is largest (-1) at d_H = 0 and decreases monotonically in d_H.
  (3) Barycentres.  For any finite set S of lifted points, B(S) is the Lorentz/Karcher barycentre: init m = lift of the normalised Euclidean mean of S, then repeat 30 times  m <- exp_m( (1/|S|) * sum_{s in S} log_m(s) ), with exp/log the Lorentz exponential and logarithm at m (closed form: exp_m(v) = cosh(||v||_L) m + sinh(||v||_L) v/||v||_L, log_m(q) = arcosh(<m,q>_L) * (q - <m,q>_L m)/||q - <m,q>_L m||).  Deterministic, no parameter.
  (4) Training quantities only.  Training split T = the list of training pairs (s,t).  For a training query item q, H_q = the multiset of items paired with q in T (its full training history; skip q if H_q is empty).  mu_q = B({p_h : h in H_q}).  For each level-1 cell c with at least one training item, gamma_c = B({p_i : i in T-split, c1(i)=c}), and pi_c = |{i in T-split : c1(i)=c}| / |T-split|.  Let C = {c : pi_c > 0}, K+ = |C|.
  (5) Logit and posterior.  l_{qc} = <mu_q, gamma_c>_L / T  with T = tau (the reference's own frozen temperature; if the reference stores only a ball radius R = tanh(tau), use T = artanh(R)).  Posterior over the whole cell population:  p(c|q) = pi_c * exp(l_{qc}/T) / sum_{c' in C} pi_c' * exp(l_{qc'}/T).
  (6) Score.  m_q = log p(c1(q)|q) - log pi_{c1(q)}  (=  l_{q,c1(q)}/T  -  logsumexp_{c in C}( log pi_c + l_{qc}/T )).  The metric is
        M = (1/|Q|) * sum_{q in Q} m_q ,   Q = training queries with H_q non-empty.
  Higher is better. One number, no thresholds. Degenerate cases: K+ <= 1 gives M = 0 exactly (a one-code table scores 0).
metrics.inputs: (a) the exported Stage-2 SID table, item_id -> integer codes per level (only level 1 is read); (b) the frozen Issue #126 behaviour reference, i.e. the per-item source representation array x_i (N x d) and its frozen temperature tau; (c) the TRAINING split pair list. Nothing else - no validation pair, no test pair, no recall, no Stage-3 artefact.
metrics.geometry: The whole computation lives on the Lorentz hyperboloid of constant curvature kappa = -1 (unit ball). Curvature enters in three load-bearing places: the exp map exp_0(tau x) that decides how far out in the ball each item sits; the Lorentzian inner product <mu_q,gamma_c>_L = -cosh(d_H) which is the only source of the logits, so separation is measured by a geodesic distance, not a dot product; and the geodesic (Karcher) barycentres, which are Frechet means in the ball and have no Euclidean counterpart. Because cosh grows exponentially, a cell one unit of hyperbolic distance further away is suppressed by a factor e^{-(cosh d2 - cosh d1)/T} - that exponential suppression of the tail is precisely the curvature effect and it is what makes the posterior concentrate without any tuned sharpness.
metrics.why: Two things are known from the 97 pairs. (i) Statistics of the partition alone do not track recall, because they never look at what the items are. (ii) Contrast statistics on the frozen reference do track it (+0.70 for HBAA vs +0.634 for Q_H), because a cell that is close to where the item's own behaviour history points is a cell whose ten retrieved neighbours will be the right items. This metric keeps (ii) and adds the two pieces of information HBAA throws away. First, the query is the geodesic barycentre of the FULL training history, not a single anchor, so a query is scored against the region of behaviour space its whole history occupies. Second, the negatives are not averaged: the reference is asked for a full posterior over all K+ cells at the reference's own temperature, and the score is the posterior mass it puts on the positive cell - an argmax-like readout that is sensitive to the whole negative distribution (a positive that beats the mean negative but is outranked by 40% of cells is penalised, which a mean-of-ten margin cannot see). Third, and unlike every likelihood tried so far, the mass is divided by the cell's own training prior pi, i.e. it is a pointwise mutual information between "what the reference says" and "what the code says". That denominator is a closed-form size-matched null, so a table cannot win by collapsing: the best attainable score is mean_q log(1/pi_{c1(q)}), which is log 2 = 0.693 for a balanced two-cell table and log 256 = 5.545 for a balanced 256-cell table. Collapse is therefore structurally unprofitable, and resolution is rewarded, without a second number or a capacity correction. What it adds over Q_H: Q_H scores a prefix by its own geometry with no query and no contrast; this scores the code by how much the reference's behaviour geometry, conditioned on the item's full history, prefers that cell over what the code's own base rate already implies. Over HBAA: HBAA's Delta is linear in four geodesic distances (algebraically it is half the sum of the origin-margin and the query-margin), it sees exactly two points, and it is unbounded and scale-sensitive; this one is curvature-exact (cosh saturation over the whole cell population), uses all K+ cells with their priors, and is bounded above by mean log(1/pi), so it cannot be inflated by representation scale.
metrics.compute: d ~ 64, K <= 256, N = 24587, |Q| <= 24587, average history length ~10. Lift: O(N d). Cell and query barycentres: 30 iterations of a matrix product each, O(30 N d) = ~5e7 flops total, done once per table. Logits: one (|Q| x (d+1)) by ((d+1) x K+) product = 4e8 flops, plus a row-wise logsumexp over <= 256 columns. Memory peak 24587 x 256 float32 = 25 MB. Fully vectorised this is a few seconds; well inside one minute, single core, CPU only.
metrics.risks: (1) Temperature mis-scaling: if tau is not the scalar Issue #126 actually used, the posterior becomes either saturated (M degenerates to a hard argmax with log-odds) or flat (M -> 0 for every table); it is one global constant per reference, identical for all 97 tables, so it changes the level of M but only mildly its rank order - still, it is the main fragility and must be taken verbatim from the reference, never fitted. (2) Level-1 only: at level 2+ the cell centroids collapse onto items, so the posterior becomes an item lookup and the prior pi re-inflates the score; this metric deliberately does not use levels 2+. (3) Sparse histories: queries with |H_q| < 2 give noisy mu_q; they are included (|H_q| >= 1) but a table whose training pairs are mostly singletons dilutes the signal toward 0. (4) Cells with very few training items get unstable gamma_c; they are kept because dropping them by a size threshold would be a tuned parameter. (5) A reference whose source side is itself nearly isotropic makes all gamma_c nearly equal, so all logits nearly equal and M nearly the mean over q of log(1/pi) minus a constant - a positive but low-variance artefact; this is visible as a near-zero spread of M across the 97 tables.
metrics.failure_mode: It must be worst on the table where level-1 is a fixed balanced random relabelling (e.g. a hash of the item id into 256 equal blocks): then gamma_c is a barycentre of a random subsample, all gamma_c sit near the ball centre with almost identical distances to mu_q, the posterior returns to the prior pi_c, and m_q = log p - log pi -> 0 for every q, so M ~ 0 with no variance. It is equally worst on the single-code table (K+ = 1, M = 0 by definition) and on any table whose level-1 blocks are random with respect to behaviour but perfectly balanced (so no prior tilt can rescue it).

metrics.title: Null-corrected hyperbolic surprisal of the true successor's level-1 cell.
metrics.formula:
Notation. N = number of rows of the exported SID table; item i carries level-1 code L1(i) in {0..255}. Cells C = {c : n_c > 0}, n_c = #{i : L1(i) = c}, K1 = |C| <= 256. P = the set of DISTINCT ordered pairs (a,b) of the TRAINING split, m = |P|. Frozen Issue #126 reference: source vector s_i and target vector t_i in R^d per item, plus its frozen softmax temperature tau > 0. All logs natural.

Curvature and ball: K = 1/tau^2 (derived from the reference's own temperature, no free parameter); B_K = {x : ||x|| < 1/sqrt(K)}.

Scales, TRAIN only: sigma_s = median{||s_i|| : i occurs in P}, sigma_t = median{||t_i|| : i occurs in P}; if a sigma is 0 set it to 1.

Ball map (exponential map at the origin): phi_s(x) = (1/sqrt(K)) * tanh( (sqrt(K)/2) * ||x||/sigma_s ) * x/||x||, phi_s(0) = 0; phi_t is the same with sigma_t.

Poincare distance: d_H(u,v) = (1/sqrt(K)) * arcosh( 1 + 2K||u-v||^2 / ((1 - K||u||^2)(1 - K||v||^2)) ).

Mobius addition: u (+) v = [ (1 + 2K<u,v> + K||v||^2) u + (1 - K||u||^2) v ] / [ 1 + 2K<u,v> + K^2||u||^2||v||^2 ].
log_u(y) = (2/sqrt(K)) * artanh( sqrt(K)*||(-u)(+)y|| ) * (-u)(+)y / ||(-u)(+)y||.
exp_u(v) = u (+) ( (1/sqrt(K)) * tanh( sqrt(K)*||v||/2 ) * v/||v|| ).

Cell representative, target side: mu_c = argmin_{mu in B_K} sum_{i in cell c, i in TRAIN} d_H(mu, phi_t(t_i))^2, computed by Karcher iteration: mu^(0) = medoid of the cell (argmin_{i in c} sum_{j in c} d_H(phi_t(t_i), phi_t(t_j))), then exactly 32 updates mu <- exp_mu( (1/n_c) * sum_{i in c} log_mu(phi_t(t_i)) ).

Train mass: w_c = n_c^tr / sum_{c'} n_{c'}^tr, where n_c^tr = number of TRAIN items in cell c.

Per pair (a,b) in P: q = phi_s(s_a); d_c = d_H(q, mu_c) for every c in C; p(c) = sum_{c' : d_{c'} >= d_c} w_{c'}; p+ = p(L1(b));
  e(a,b) = [ -log p+ ] - [ sum_c w_c * ( -log p(c) ) ].

SCORE = (1/m) * sum_{(a,b) in P} e(a,b). Convention: SCORE = 0 when K1 = 1 or m = 0. Higher is better. A code-blind table of any size scores exactly 0; the ceiling is about log(1/min_c w_c) nats (about 4.8 for 256 balanced cells).
metrics.inputs: (1) the exported SID table, item id -> level-1 integer code (only level 1 is read); (2) the frozen Issue #126 behaviour reference: s_i, t_i per item and its temperature tau; (3) the TRAINING pair list. Nothing else: no validation pair, no test pair, no recall value, no Stage 3 artefact.
metrics.geometry: constant negative curvature K = 1/tau^2, taken from the reference's frozen temperature, so no constant is tuned. Curvature enters four times, each load-bearing: (i) the tanh squashing of the ball map, which is the exponential map at the origin and makes radial distance grow hyperbolically; (ii) the ball radius 1/sqrt(K) and the arcosh Poincare distance, which is not a rescaling of the Euclidean one; (iii) the Mobius-add / log / exp Karcher barycentre, so a cell representative is a true hyperbolic Frechet mean of the reference's target points, not a Euclidean average; (iv) the ordering of d_c that defines p(c), evaluated in that distance.
metrics.why: Stage 3 enumerates SID prefixes and scores candidates with the reference, so Recall@10 is high exactly when the true successor's level-1 bucket is one of the few buckets the beam spends mass on. The quantity that decides this is how much candidate mass the level-1 code removes for a real query, measured in the reference's own geometry, which is p+ and its excess over chance. Over Q_H: Q_H is a statistic of the partition alone, so two tables with identical level-1 occupancy but different placement relative to the reference are indistinguishable to it; here the query is the reference's source point and the representative is the barycentre of the reference's TARGET points, so the number asks whether quantisation preserved the reference's successor field. Over HBAA: HBAA reduces each item's history to one barycentre and its negatives to a mean over ten, which is lossy twice over - the barycentre of a multi-modal history sits between its modes and far from every one of them, and a mean of ten negatives throws away the shape of the negative distribution. This metric keeps every training pair as its own query (the finest, un-coarsened use of the whole training history), uses the full negative CDF rather than a mean, and uses the target side of the reference, which HBAA never touches. Over the measured failures: raw surprisal -log p+ is monotone in K1, which is exactly why hyp_hsoftmax_path tracked bucket count at -0.78 and blew up on the 12-, 3- and 2-code tables; subtracting the size-biased null sum_c w_c(-log p(c)) makes the statistic exactly 0 for every code-blind table of any size, so collapse and shattering are neutralised analytically instead of by a tuned penalty. Two facts I checked by hand make the null exact: for a code-blind assignment E[p] = 0.5(1 - sum_c w_c^2) and E[e] = 0, and for the one-code table p = p(c) = 1 so e = 0.
metrics.compute: dominant cost is the m x K1 hyperbolic distance matrix, m = |P| pairs, K1 <= 256, d = 64 reals: 2e5 x 256 x 64 = 3e9 flops, and the arcosh form needs no log or exp, so about 10-20 s in vectorised float64 numpy on 24587 items. Barycentres cost 32 x 24587 x 64 = 5e7 flops, under 1 s. Ranking 256 distances per query is m x 256 log 256, a few seconds. Memory is one length-K1 mass vector plus the m x K1 score matrix, which can be streamed in row blocks. Total comfortably under one minute.
metrics.risks: (1) it assumes s_i and t_i live in one shared ball, as HBAA's (u_h | mu_b) reduction also does; if the reference is a two-tower model with non-shared geometry the distances are meaningless and the metric is noise. (2) Median scaling puts the norm tail near the boundary; guard 1 - K||u||^2 >= 1e-12 so arcosh stays finite. (3) Without deduplication of P a few heavy pairs dominate the mean; dedup is part of the definition. (4) If one successor is overwhelmingly popular and its cell's barycentre happens to be central, the score is inflated by popularity - partly real recall signal, partly a confound. (5) The conservative >= tie rule slightly deflates p+ on very coarse tables. (6) It reads only level 1, so it cannot see any improvement made below the root.
metrics.failure_mode: worst on the one-code table - all 24587 items in code 0 gives p+ = 1 and p(c) = 1, hence e = 0 and the score sits exactly on the floor 0; the same 0 is reached by any size-preserving random relabel of a good table, so a collapse is never rewarded. Its honest blind spot is the opposite direction: any two tables sharing the level-1 partition score identically, so a good root partition with a randomised level 2+ refinement is scored as if it were good. That blindness is deliberate - from level 2 the prefix is nearly an item identifier (Q_H drops to +0.287 at level 2 and +0.393 at level 3) and the remaining variation is noise.
